question: If secA + tanA = (5)/(2), then what is secA-tanA?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ We know the standard trigonometric identity: sec²A − tan²A = 1 This expands to: (secA − tanA) × (secA + tanA) = 1 Thus, (secA − tanA) is always the reciprocal of (secA + tanA). ⇒ secA − tanA = 1 ÷ (5/2) = 2/5 **∴ The correct answer is 2/5.**
